title: Adaptive batcher tuner overapply incident and recovery playbook
creator: Priya Singh
summary: Post-incident analysis and an operational playbook after an Optimize auto-tuner misapplied an aggressive batching/cache configuration, causing a transient cost spike and CPU/latency regressions across hosted region us-east-1. This ticket consolidates the timeline, root cause, immediate mitigations, and an actionable safe-apply/rollback runbook with tests and owners.
incident_timeline:
2025-02-14 09:12 UTC - Tuner scheduled a staged apply: increased batch_size target from 8 to 32 and disabled prefix-level KV caching for short-tail requests.
2025-02-14 09:18 UTC - Canary traffic (2% of requests) reported elevated latency P95 (from 85ms -> 180ms) and token throughput drop.
2025-02-14 09:20 UTC - Cost alert triggered: estimated per-minute token cost increased by ~42% in canary cohort.
2025-02-14 09:25 UTC - Tuner continued rollout to 50% due to automated 'improvement' metric (average token cost per response) showing apparent gains in long-tail tests.
2025-02-14 09:34 UTC - Platform alerting: backlog queue depth rose on serving nodes; autoscaler spun new nodes but cold-starts increased P99 latency.
2025-02-14 09:40 UTC - SRE performed emergency rollback to previous config; by 09:48 UTC latency and cost trends recovered to baseline.
2025-02-14 10:10 UTC - Postmortem initiated; key stakeholders notified (Product, Eng, SRE, Optimize team).
impact_metrics:
Duration: ~18 minutes from first canary anomaly to full rollback.
Cost: Peak short-term token cost rate increased by 38-45% in us-east-1 for affected service tier. Estimated incremental spend: $1,900 for the 18-minute window.
Reliability: P95 latency regressed by ~110ms during peak. Error rate did not exceed normal thresholds.
Customers: No user-facing errors; a subset of latency-sensitive internal customers (low-latency partners) reported degradations but no data loss.
root_causes:
1) Metric misalignment: the tuner objective prioritized amortized token-cost-per-response using a synthetic long-tail dataset which over-weighted batching efficiency and under-weighted latency SLOs.
2) Incomplete safety gates: rollout policy allowed rapid ramp (2% -> 50%) based solely on cost-based improvement without latency-senstive checks or backpressure signals (queue depth/P99).
3) Cache eviction oversight: the tuner disabled prefix/KV caching for certain short-tailed paths assuming batch gains would dominate; this caused cache misses and CPU pressure on hot paths.
4) Insufficient canary fidelity: canary traffic didn't mirror low-latency partner traffic; test harness lacked representative concurrency and cold-start profiles.
immediate_mitigations:
- Emergency rollback to previous config (completed 09:40–09:48 UTC).
- Re-enabled prefix-level KV caching for all short-tail routes.
- Added temporary throttle preventing any auto-tuner staged applies >5% per 10 minutes.
- Manual audit of tuner experiments that had staged applies in the last 72 hours.
long_term_mitigations:
- Revise tuner objective to include explicit latency SLO penalties (P95 and P99) and queue depth constraints.
- Implement dual-metric canary gating: require both 'cost improvement' and 'latency non-regression' to proceed.
- Add hysteresis windows and minimum observation time (10–15 minutes) before ramping >10%.
- Improve cache-aware tuning: ensure KV cache policies are simulated in the dry-run harness and use conservative cache-disable defaults.
- Expand canary traffic fidelity by including low-latency partner profiles and cold-start scenarios in the testbed.
- Add a cost-exposure limiter that prevents total per-region cost rate from increasing >15% over baseline during staged rollout.
safe_apply_playbook:
Purpose: Provide an operator and automated-safe path for Optimize automated config applies that balances cost wins with reliability.
Steps: 
1) Dry-run phase (sim): run tuner change in simulation using 1:1 playback of recent production traffic plus synthetic low-latency partner traces. Require pass on: no P95 regression >10ms, queue depth <= baseline+15%, and confirmed cache hit-rate degradation <5%.
2) Canary deploy (control-plane gated): create a canary cohort constrained to 1% traffic for 15 minutes. Monitor these signals: cost-per-response, P95, P99, queue depth, baseline cache hit-rate.
3) Canary gating: Only allow ramp if BOTH cost delta <= -5% and latency deltas within thresholds (P95 delta <= +10ms, P99 delta <= +25ms). Require human approval if cost wins but latency borderline.
4) Staged ramps: 1% -> 5% -> 12% -> 25% -> 50% with minimum hold time of 10 minutes at each step and checks at every stage.
5) Automated abort: if any metric breaches defined thresholds (cost exposure >15%, P95 regresses >30ms, queue depth >baseline+50%), auto-roll back to last stable config and page on-call.
6) Post-apply audit: run a 24-hour automated audit comparing expected vs observed cost/latency. If drift >10% vs dry-run projection, trigger human review.
Observability: Create a dashboard that shows per-stage metrics and a single boolean 'SafeApplyReady' that must be true to proceed.
rollback_playbook:
Purpose: Fast, reliable rollback and validation procedure.
Steps: 
1) Detection: Alerting rules detect regression (cost exposure, P95/P99, queue depth).
2) Immediate actuation: If threshold breach is critical (as defined in SafeApply gating), the system invokes an automated rollback to the previous stable configuration.
3) Verification window: After rollback, hold traffic at 100% stable config and verify P95/P99 and cost trends for a 6-minute verification window (two GC cycles/caches warm).
4) Post-rollback triage: SRE/Optimize run root-cause checklist and collect playback traces.
5) Containment: If rollback fails or metrics degrade, divert traffic to fallback region/pool and initiate incident commander (IC) process.
6) Communication: Notify stakeholders via incident channel with rollback time, reason, and next steps.
Note: Rollback must be idempotent and reversible; require a post-rollback 'health check' pass before any further applies are attempted.
runbook_checklist: Confirm dry-run simulation has representative low-latency and cold-start traffic
Verify SafeApplyReady boolean is true in control plane
Ensure canary cohort allocation is isolated and observability hooks are enabled
Confirm alerts for cost exposure, P95, P99, queue depth, and cache hit-rate are active
Have human approver (Optimize owner) assigned before ramp beyond 5%
Document expected cost delta and latency thresholds in canary change description
